name: Switched after registration
short: What the paper reports is not what was registered, and the change is not explained.

ref.cite: Goldacre et al. (2019). COMPare: a prospective cohort study correcting and monitoring 58 misreported trials in real time. Trials.

name: HARKing
short: A hypothesis written after the results, presented as if it came first.

ref.cite: Kerr (1998). HARKing: hypothesizing after the results are known. Personality and Social Psychology Review.

name: p-hacking
short: Many analyses tried, and only the one that reached significance reported.

ref.cite: Simmons et al. (2011). False-positive psychology. Psychological Science.

name: Overclaiming
short: The conclusion claims more than the design can show.

ref.cite: Boutron & Ravaud (2018). Misrepresentation and distortion of research in biomedical literature. PNAS.

name: Predictable allocation
short: Whoever enrols participants can foresee or steer the next assignment.

ref.cite: Schulz et al. (1995). Empirical evidence of bias: dimensions of methodological quality associated with estimates of treatment effects in controlled trials. JAMA.

name: Exposure after outcome
short: The 'cause' was measured or counted after the outcome had begun.

ref.cite: Hill (1965). The environment and disease: association or causation? Proceedings of the Royal Society of Medicine.

name: Interviewer with power
short: The person collecting the data has power over the participants.

ref.cite: Berger (2015). Now I see it, now I don't: researcher's position and reflexivity in qualitative research. Qualitative Research.

name: Partial verification
short: Only some participants got the reference standard, chosen by their test result.

name: Narrow search
short: Too few sources searched, so relevant studies are missed.

name: Hand-picked participants
short: Staff chose who took part by unwritten criteria, so results may not carry over.

name: Selective loss to follow-up
short: The people lost differ from those who stayed, in ways that matter.

name: Unsuitable controls
short: Controls do not come from the population that produced the cases.

name: Self-selected sample
short: Whoever chose to answer, so the sample can't stand for the population.

ref.cite: Hernán et al. (2004). A structural approach to selection bias. Epidemiology.

name: Saturation not reached
short: Data collection stopped for practical reasons, yet saturation is claimed.

ref.cite: Saunders et al. (2018). Saturation in qualitative research: exploring its conceptualization and operationalization. Quality & Quantity.

name: Spectrum bias
short: Clear-cut cases compared with healthy people, leaving out the hard cases.

name: Unpublished studies left out
short: Only published studies count, and those lean towards positive results.

name: Unreported exclusions
short: Animals or participants dropped from the analysis without a word.

short: The people judging the outcome knew who got what.

name: Recall bias
short: Cases and controls remember past exposures differently.

short: A home-made measure with no evidence that it captures what it claims.

ref.cite: Flake & Fried (2020). Measurement schmeasurement: questionable measurement practices and how to avoid them. Advances in Methods and Practices in Psychological Science.

name: Single coder, no audit trail
short: One person coded everything, and nobody can follow how.

name: Unblinded test reading
short: The test was read by someone who already knew the right answer.

name: No risk-of-bias assessment
short: Included studies were never judged for bias.

short: Only participants who stuck to the plan were analysed.

name: Uncontrolled confounding
short: A factor behind both exposure and outcome was left unadjusted.

ref.cite: Kyriacou & Lewis (2016). Confounding by indication in clinical research. JAMA.

name: Missing data ignored
short: Incomplete records dropped, although who is missing is not random.

ref.cite: Sterne et al. (2009). Multiple imputation for missing data in epidemiological and clinical research: potential and pitfalls. BMJ.

name: Themes = interview questions
short: The 'themes' are the headings of the interview guide.

ref.cite: Braun & Clarke (2006). Using thematic analysis in psychology. Qualitative Research in Psychology.

name: Data-driven cut-off
short: The cut-off was tuned on the same data used to judge accuracy.

name: Unexplored heterogeneity

name: Pseudoreplication
short: Repeated measurements of one unit counted as independent units.

name: Missing detail
short: A step is reported too vaguely for readers to judge or repeat it.

name: Intervention not described
short: The intervention is not described well enough for anyone to repeat it.

name: No confidence interval
short: An effect comes with a p-value but no confidence interval, so its size and precision are unclear.
